errors.text: The proposed effect has the wrong direction: enhanced L12 ordering is presented as protection against toughness loss, whereas the target mechanism identifies maximal L12 ordering near 600 °C as a cause of embrittlement.

The mechanism invokes reduced defect mobility and suppression of radiation-induced segregation, although the problem concerns thermal aging without irradiation and the cited evidence does not support this causal pathway.
The hypothesis omits the coupled role of jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, dislocation pile-ups, stress concentration, and plastic instability.
It fails to predict the defining non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response and the recovery near 750 °C.

The experiment measures generic thermal stability and mechanical properties but cannot distinguish the proposed mechanism from precipitation strengthening, phase-fraction changes, or phase-boundary-controlled embrittlement.
